In April 2003, 12-month inflation dropped to 0.3% against 0.6% in March 2003, mainly as a result of fuel prices, domestic running expenses and energy prices growing more slowly than a month ago.

In April 2003, the annual growth rate of the PPI amounted to 2.9% Production price against 3.6% in March.
In comparison to the previous month, the prices of industrial output fell by 0.4%, while they rose by 0.9% in March.
The slower PPI growth stemmed from the falling prices in industrial processing (mainly in coking and petroleum refining, where prices fell by 11%).
This decline was mainly a result of lower oil prices on the world market.
Had oil prices not gone down and the zloty not weakened, annual PPI growth in April 2003 would have been 3.1%-3.2%.
